reranked_evidence.snippet: # Salman Rushdie Testifies At Terrorism Trial Of The Man Convicted Of Stabbing Him. (AP) — Four years after being stabbed on an amphitheater stage, Salman Rushdie sat across a courtroom from his convicted attacker Thursday and told jurors for a second time about the ambush that nearly killed him. Then “I was on the stage, lying down, with an enormous pool of blood all around me,” Rushdie testified. A Buffalo federal court jury watched Rushdie fixedly as he testified — and at one point removed his glasses to show his unseeing right eye — at Hadi Matar’s terrorism trial. Matar already was convicted of a state-level attempted murder charge in the 2022 attack at a cultural institution where Rushdie was poised to speak about threats to writers and artists. Matar’s attorneys have argued that prosecutors can’t prove his intent or mindset at the time of the attack — a key element in their claim that it was an act of terrorism motivated by allegiance to Iran’s government and the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group.
